card.title: 8e MAROCAINS

card.flavorText: The 8th Regiment of Moroccan Tirailleurs was part of the 2nd Moroccan Division (French: 2e Division d'Infanterie Marocaine, 2e DIM), formed in 1943 after the Allied liberation of French North Africa, and part of the Army of Africa (French: Armée d'Afrique). It was the first French division to land in Italy, where it fought in the Monte Cassino campaign. The unit participated in several key battles, including San Michele de Pantano, Mainarde, and Monte Croce. On May 11th, 1944, the division captured Monte Majo in the Battle of Garigliano, and later marched through Rome on June 15th. The division then advanced to Siena and Florence. Though it missed the initial invasion of Southern France, it arrived in late August 1944, liberating Briançon and Modane. It broke through German defenses at the Belfort Gap, captured several towns, and entered Belfort. After reaching the Doller and Thur Valleys, it helped eliminate the Colmar Pocket, crossed the Rhine in March 1945, and continued into Germany, entering Karlsruhe, Pforzheim, and later Austria. The 2nd Moroccan Division was deactivated in August 1945 after being decorated numerous times for its actions during the war.
